sentences.en: Scott Shane on the moral complexities of Julian Assange.
sentences.zh: 斯科特·沙恩谈朱利安·阿桑奇的道德复杂性。

sentences.en: It's Monday, April 15th.
sentences.zh: 今天是4月15日，星期一。

sentences.en: Scott, tell us what happened in London on Thursday.
sentences.zh: 斯科特，请告诉我们周四在伦敦发生了什么。

sentences.en: So, a large squad of police showed up at the Embassy of Ecuador, where Julian Assange has been holed up for seven years, not leaving the building.
sentences.zh: 当时，一大队警察出现在厄瓜多尔驻英国大使馆，朱利安·阿桑奇在那里躲了七年，一步未出。

sentences.en: And the Ecuadorian authorities got a little sick of him.
sentences.zh: 厄瓜多尔当局有点受够他了。

sentences.en: He would skateboard, and they complained about his skateboarding, the noise, the damage he was doing to the building.
sentences.zh: 他会玩滑板，他们抱怨他的滑板声、噪音，以及他对建筑造成的损害。

sentences.en: He would skateboard inside the embassy?
sentences.zh: 他在大使馆里面玩滑板？

sentences.en: You know, I mean, the guy was there for seven years.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我的意思是，这家伙在那呆了七年。

sentences.en: He couldn't go outside.
sentences.zh: 他不能去外面。

sentences.en: He would play with a soccer ball and throw it and kick it against the wall.
sentences.zh: 他会玩足球，把它扔来扔去，或者踢向墙壁。

sentences.en: And they got tired of that.
sentences.zh: 他们对这个感到厌烦了。

sentences.en: A security guard came to take the soccer ball away, accused him of not taking care of his cat, not taking care of his bathroom.
sentences.zh: 一名保安来收走足球，指责他没有照顾好猫，没有打理好洗手间。

sentences.en: So, it was almost like a bad scene in a college dorm, I think.
sentences.zh: 所以，我觉得这有点像大学宿舍里的糟糕场景。

sentences.en: We've got breaking news for you.
sentences.zh: 我们为您插播一条突发新闻。

sentences.en: And I have to tell you, the pictures are shocking from London today, where Julian Assange's long standoff with international authorities is finally over.
sentences.zh: 我不得不说，今天来自伦敦的画面令人震惊，朱利安·阿桑奇与国际当局长期对峙终于结束了。

sentences.en: Finally, the Ecuadorian authorities had made the decision to evict him.
sentences.zh: 最终，厄瓜多尔当局做出了驱逐他的决定。

sentences.en: And there, the British police authorities were there waiting to accept the body, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 英国警方当局则在那里等待，可以说是来接收这具“尸体”。

sentences.en: And he resisted, so they carried him out.
sentences.zh: 他进行了反抗，于是他们把他抬了出来。

sentences.en: Oh, my God, look at him.
sentences.zh: 天哪，快看他。

sentences.en: Look at him.
sentences.zh: 快看他。

sentences.en: The beard, I have not seen him looking like that.
sentences.zh: 那胡子，我从未见过他这副模样。

sentences.en: Clearly not being taken willingly.
sentences.zh: 显然不是自愿离开的。

sentences.en: He's being dragged.
sentences.zh: 他被拖走了。

sentences.en: And he was quite disheveled, white beard.
sentences.zh: 他非常不修边幅，留着白胡子。

sentences.en: Look at how many people it's taking to take him down.
sentences.zh: 看看带走他需要多少人。

sentences.en: He's not going willingly.
sentences.zh: 他并不情愿离开。

sentences.en: He looks like
sentences.zh: 他看起来像

sentences.en: Rip Van Winkle.
sentences.zh: 里普·范·温克尔。

sentences.en: And he was yelling, we can resist, we must resist, you can resiSt. And they sort of shoveled him into a gray police van.
sentences.zh: 他在大喊：我们能反抗，我们必须反抗，你们可以反抗。然后他们把他塞进了一辆灰色警车里。

sentences.en: Julian Assange now faces a single U.S.
sentences.zh: 朱利安·阿桑奇现在面临一项美国

sentences.en: federal conspiracy charge related to one of the largest ever leaks of government secrets.
sentences.zh: 联邦共谋指控，该指控与历史上最大规模的政府机密泄露事件之一有关。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: is seeking to extradite him.
sentences.zh: 正寻求引渡他。

sentences.en: But Assange is vowing to fight it.
sentences.zh: 但阿桑奇发誓要抗争到底。

sentences.en: So you had this scene, which in some ways is quite appropriate, of Julian Assange, the founder of WikiLeaks, against the world, against the powerful state,
sentences.zh: 所以你看到了这样一个场景，在某种程度上非常贴切：维基解密创始人朱利安·阿桑奇对抗全世界，对抗强大国家，

sentences.en: taking his stand and trying to rally his troops.
sentences.zh: 坚定立场并试图凝聚他的支持者。

sentences.en: And Scott, what's the significance of this moment?
sentences.zh: 斯科特，这一时刻的意义何在？

sentences.en: Well, this was the end of a 10-year kind of global saga that involved the U.S., the U.K., Ecuador,
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一场长达十年的全球大戏的终结，其中涉及美国、英国、厄瓜多尔、

sentences.en: Sweden, Russia, everybody with their own particular interest in Julian Assange and WikiLeaks.
sentences.zh: 瑞典、俄罗斯，每个人对朱利安·阿桑奇和维基解密都有着各自的利益诉求。

sentences.en: And I hesitate to say it's the end, but it's at least a milestone in the very colorful career of
sentences.zh: 我 hesitant（犹豫）说这是终结，但它至少是朱利安·阿桑奇

sentences.en: Julian Assange.
sentences.zh: 多姿多彩的职业生涯中的一个里程碑。

sentences.en: WikiLeaks had been founded by Julian Assange, this former hacker from Australia, in 2006.
sentences.zh: 维基解密是由这位前澳大利亚黑客朱利安·阿桑奇于2006年创立的。

sentences.en: So these are, as far as we can tell, classical whistleblowers.
sentences.zh: 据我们所知，这些人是典型的泄密者。

sentences.en: And we have a number of ways for them to get information to us.
sentences.zh: 我们有多种渠道让他们向我们提供信息。

sentences.en: They would collect whistleblower documents, various kinds of secret documents, and put them up on the web for everybody to see.
sentences.zh: 他们会收集泄密者的文件，各种机密文件，并将它们放到网上供所有人查看。

sentences.en: We get information in the mail, read it like a regular news organization, release it to the public, and then defend ourselves against the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我们通过邮件获取信息，像普通新闻机构一样阅读它，向公众发布，然后应对来自美国的压力。

sentences.en: But they hadn't really made much of a splash.
sentences.zh: 但他们当时并没有引起多大轰动。

sentences.en: No one had really heard of them.
sentences.zh: 当时没人听说过他们。

sentences.en: They hadn't gotten much media attention until 2010, when they got the mother load essentially delivered to them by
sentences.zh: 直到2010年，切尔西·曼宁（当时名为布拉德利·曼宁，伊拉克战场上一名感到厌烦的美国陆军二等兵、低级别情报分析员）基本上把海量核心资料交给了他们，他们才真正受到媒体关注。

sentences.en: Chelsea Manning, then known as Bradley Manning, this bored army private low-level intelligence analyst in Iraq.
sentences.zh: （注：此处原文对应调整已在中文自然连贯表达中处理）

sentences.en: And they were extremely happy to hear from her and to handle her documents.
sentences.zh: 他们听到她的消息并处理她的文件时感到非常高兴。

sentences.en: And where were you in this moment?
sentences.zh: 那一刻你在哪里？

sentences.en: So I was in the Times-Washington Bureau, and a team of us were sort of on the receiving end of this giant document dump from WikiLeaks.
sentences.zh: 当时我在《时报》华盛顿分社，我们团队负责接收维基解密倾倒的海量文件。

sentences.en: There were first the war logs, which were sort of on the ground secret reports from the troops and about the troops in Afghanistan and Iraq.
sentences.zh: 首先是战争日志，这基本上是驻阿富汗和伊拉克部队关于前线及部队内部的秘密报告。

sentences.en: And then there were a quarter million confidential diplomatic cables, essentially the letters that diplomats send
sentences.zh: 然后是二十五万份机密外交电报，也就是世界各地大使馆的外交官

sentences.en: back from embassies around the world to the State Department in Washington, and the instructions from the State Department out to the field.
sentences.zh: 发回华盛顿国务院的信件，以及国务院下发到各外地机构的指示。

sentences.en: And no one had seen anything like this many confidential military and diplomatic documents before.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，没有人见过如此数量庞大的军事和外交机密文件。

sentences.en: Well, tell me how you're thinking about what Assange is doing here by releasing so many secretive diplomatic documents and the role that you as a journalist are playing in that.
sentences.zh: 那么，请告诉我，你如何看待阿桑奇通过发布如此多的机密外交电报所做的事情，以及你作为一名记者在其中扮演的角色？

sentences.en: I think you feel very ambivalent about a guy like Assange.
sentences.zh: 我想你对阿桑奇这样的人感觉非常矛盾。

sentences.en: He's somewhere on the boundary between a source and a kind of journalistic collaborator.
sentences.zh: 他介于消息来源和某种新闻合作伙伴之间。

sentences.en: What was different about this was usually your source is a government official, and they kind of know the rules of the game, and you know the rules of the
sentences.zh: 不同之处在于，通常你的消息来源是政府官员，他们有点了解游戏规则，你也知道规则，

sentences.en: game, and they know the risk they're running, and so on.
sentences.zh: 他们也知道自己要承担的风险，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Now we're dealing with somebody who is not only not a government official, but a very freewheeling, sort of ideologically driven, fairly eccentric character.
sentences.zh: 而现在我们打交道的人不仅不是政府官员，而且是一个非常自由散漫、带有意识形态驱动色彩、相当古怪的角色。

sentences.en: Julian Assange had pronounced this theory, I guess you'd call it, that the powerful were hoarding information and keeping it from the people.
sentences.zh: 朱利安·阿桑奇提出了这样一个理论，你可以这么称呼它：权贵们在囤积信息，并向民众隐瞒这些信息。

sentences.en: Information that organizations are spending economic effort into concealing, that's a really good signal that when the information gets out, there's a hope of it doing some good.
sentences.zh: 那些各个机构付出经济成本去掩盖的信息，正是一个强烈的信号：一旦这些信息被公之于众，就有望带来一些好的改变。

sentences.en: And he wanted to set it free.
sentences.zh: 他想让这些信息重获自由。

sentences.en: The goal is justice.
sentences.zh: 目标是正义。

sentences.en: The method is transparency.
sentences.zh: 方法是透明。

sentences.en: It's important not to confuse the goal and the method.
sentences.zh: 重要的是不要混淆目标和方法。

sentences.en: So he was inclined in a maybe, you know, oversimplified way to just throw everything out there versus a more traditional journalistic approach, which is, first of all, you know,
sentences.zh: 因此，他可能倾向于用一种也许你知道的、过于简单化的方式，把所有东西都抛出去；而传统的新闻方法则是，首先，你知道的，

sentences.en: we don't want to actually get people killed by just putting up confidential documents.
sentences.zh: 我们不想仅仅通过公开机密文件而导致无辜人员丧生。

sentences.en: We were trying to do editing and pick and choose and be careful in what we put out there and be selective and also try to make sense of it.
sentences.zh: 我们试图进行编辑、精挑细选、谨慎发布、有所选择，并试图理清头绪。

sentences.en: So it was a complicated relationship on both sides.
sentences.zh: 因此，双方维持着一种复杂的关系。

sentences.en: But I think that tension has been present in the relationship between WikiLeaks and traditional journalism, conventional journalism, you know, since its founding.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，维基解密与传统新闻业、常规新闻业之间的这种紧张关系，你知道的，自其创立以来就一直存在。

sentences.en: And what was the response from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 当美国政府得知你们手头有这些外交电报、维基解密向你们倾倒了所有这些文件时，他们的反应是什么？

sentences.en: government once they learned that you had these diplomatic cables, that WikiLeaks had dumped all of these documents on you?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我真的给白宫打了电话，说我们有二十五万份机密

sentences.en: Well, I literally called over to the White House and said, we have a quarter million confidential
sentences.zh: 电报，我们计划发表其中的许多内容，并撰写大量关于它们的故事。

sentences.en: cables, and we plan to publish a lot of them and to write a lot of stories about them.
sentences.zh: 白宫里有人惊得差从地上跳起来。

sentences.en: And somebody peeled themselves off the ground at the White House.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 我想他们多少察觉到有什么事情正在酝酿。

sentences.en: I think they had some inkling that something was afoot.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们会回复你们。

sentences.en: They said, we'll get back to you.
sentences.zh: 他们在晚上8点左右把我们召集到国务院，我们被带到一个大房间里，

sentences.en: They summoned us to the State Department at about 8 p.m., and we were led to this big room where
sentences.zh: 那里坐着一排来自多个机构的高级官员，堪称豪华阵容，包括国防部

sentences.en: there was basically a murderer's row of senior officials from a bunch of agencies, the Defense
sentences.zh: 、中央情报局，传达的最初信息是：你们占有了赃物。

sentences.en: Department, the CIA, and the initial message was, you are in possession of stolen goods.
sentences.zh: 我们期望你们归还这些赃物——也就是这些电报，并且不要撰写任何关于它们的内容。

sentences.en: We expect you to return the stolen goods, these cables, and not to write anything about them.
sentences.zh: 随后发生了一场紧张的交流，代表我们发言的迪恩·巴凯（Dean Baquet）礼貌而坚定地表明，我们打算报道这些事情。

sentences.en: And there was a sort of tense exchange in which Dean Baquet, who was speaking for us, made it clear politely but firmly that we intended to write about these things.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，会议在这样一个共识中结束：我们会告诉他们我们打算发表哪些电报。

sentences.en: And, you know, the meeting concluded with the idea that we would tell them which cables we intended to publish.
sentences.zh: 我记得大约是下午5点

sentences.en: As I recall, it was around 5 p.m.
sentences.zh: 每天，我们与一群国务院官员之间都会进行一次电话会议，我们会挑出比如，你知道的，10份关于阿富汗的电报

sentences.en: every day, there'd be a conference call between us and a bunch of State Department officials, and we would have identified, say, you know, 10 cables
sentences.zh: 说我们打算发表，他们会让阿富汗专家在线上，

sentences.en: about Afghanistan that we intended to publish, and they would have their Afghan experts on
sentences.zh: 我们逐一过目这些电报，在某些情况下，他们会说，你知道的，

sentences.en: the line, and we would go through the cables, and they would say, in some cases, you know,
sentences.zh: 我们对第三篇没有意见，但第六篇里有三个名字我们希望你们删掉。

sentences.en: we have no problem with number three, but there are three names we'd like you to take out of cable six.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，我们会发现我们已经决定对这些名字进行脱敏处理，因为很明显，如果我们公布这些名字，人们可能会处于危险之中。

sentences.en: In some cases, we would discover that we'd already decided to redact those names because it was clear that people might be endangered if we published the name.
sentences.zh: 但同时还有一类请求，显然源于国务院的焦虑感。

sentences.en: But then there were also a class of requests that essentially were clearly coming out of a sense of anguish at the State Department.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，如果你们发表这个，会在国内激怒非常非常多的人。

sentences.en: They would say, if you publish this, it's going to really, really upset a lot of people in the country.
sentences.zh: 他们会对我们的外交官极其愤怒。

sentences.en: They're going to be extremely angry at our diplomats.
sentences.zh: 这会使关系变得紧张。

sentences.en: It will strain relations.
sentences.zh: 在几乎所有这些情况下，我们都说，听着，我们表示同情，但我们不能基于这种原因隐瞒信息，我们将继续推进。

sentences.en: And in almost all of those cases, we said, look, we're sympathetic, but we can't withhold something based on that, and we're going to go ahead.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一系列形形色色的决定。

sentences.en: So there was a whole range of decisions.
sentences.zh: 我们发表了。

sentences.en: And we published it.
sentences.zh: 它引起了极大的关注。
